reasoning: As of March 6, 2026, the Hungarian election is scheduled for April 12, 2026. Recent polling shows Tisza with an 8-12 point lead over Fidesz among decided voters, though pro-government pollsters show different results. The hybrid electoral system favors larger parties. Tisza needs a 3-5 point national vote margin to secure a majority due to constituency boundary changes. The significant divergence between government and non-government pollsters creates uncertainty. Orbán has dominated Hungarian politics for two decades, but faces his most serious challenge from Péter Magyar's Tisza Party. Given the polling lead for Tisza, undecided voters, and systemic factors, Fidesz winning most seats appears less likely than not, though the polling discrepancies and electoral system complexity introduce meaningful uncertainty.
